question: Which layer of the skin is affected in a simple first-degree (superficial) burn?
explanation: Great job! First-degree burns only touch the outer layer of skin (the epidermis), causing redness and mild pain without any blisters. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T6#GNS324_U6_T6_h1)

question: Why might a patient feel surprisingly little pain right after a very severe full-thickness burn?

options.A: The outer skin layer blocks the pain signals from traveling
options.B: Deep muscle tissue absorbs all the initial heat energy
options.C: The body releases a large amount of natural painkillers
options.D: The nerve endings in the skin have been destroyed

explanation: Spot on! Because full-thickness burns destroy the skin completely, the nerve endings that usually send pain signals to the brain are burnt away. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T6#GNS324_U6_T6_h1)

question: To help prevent tap water scald injuries at home, what is the recommended maximum water heater temperature?
explanation: You got it! Setting home water heaters to a maximum of 49 degrees Celsius (120 degrees Fahrenheit) keeps families safe from nasty scalds. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T6#GNS324_U6_T6_h2)

question: A parent is cooking soup with a toddler playing nearby. Which simple kitchen habit prevents scalds?

options.A: Turning the pot handle inward toward the back of the stove
options.B: Leaving the pot lid slightly open so steam can escape quickly
options.C: Keeping a dry dish towel draped over the front stove knobs
options.D: Placing the pot on the front right burner for easier viewing

explanation: Exactly! Turning handles toward the back stops curious little hands from grabbing them and pulling hot food down. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T6#GNS324_U6_T6_h2)

question: What makes electrical and chemical burns so tricky compared to normal flame burns?

options.A: They heal completely within twenty-four hours without scarring
options.B: They only affect the outermost layer of the dead skin cells
options.C: They never require immediate medical attention or hospital care
options.D: They frequently cause hidden internal tissue damage beneath the skin

explanation: Spot on! Electricity and chemicals can travel deep inside the body, meaning the damage under the skin is often much worse than what you see on the surface. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T6#GNS324_U6_T6_h3)

question: Why is it dangerous to pour household cleaning chemicals into empty beverage bottles?

options.A: Bottled drinks cannot hold the weight of heavy industrial-strength soap
options.B: It causes the chemical solution to evaporate and lose its cleaning power completely
options.C: The plastic material used in beverage bottles reacts poorly with standard water
options.D: It increases the risk of accidental ingestion by mistaking the chemical for a drink

explanation: That's right! Putting chemicals in drink bottles is a major cause of accidental poisoning because someone might easily mistake it for a refreshing drink. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T6#GNS324_U6_T6_h3)

question: How often should you test smoke alarm batteries in a home?
explanation: Correct! Checking smoke alarms every month ensures the batteries are active and ready to save lives in an emergency. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T6#GNS324_U6_T6_h4)

question: During a fire, why should you use the back of your hand to feel if a closed door is hot?

options.A: The palm contains thicker skin that blocks temperature perception entirely
options.B: The skin on the back of the hand is more sensitive to heat and prevents finger flexion injury
options.C: It keeps the fingers free to hold a flashlight or escape rope
options.D: It prevents soot and black ash from staining the palms of the hands

explanation: Great clinical reasoning! Using the back of your hand protects your fingers from curling up or blistering so you can still grab things and escape safely. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T6#GNS324_U6_T6_h4)

question: Why are young children at a much higher risk of severe scald burns than adults?

options.A: Their bodies contain less water to help absorb heat energy
options.B: They spend more time working directly inside commercial kitchens
options.C: Their skin is thinner and burns much faster at lower temperatures
options.D: They have faster reflexes that cause them to grab hot pans

explanation: Spot on! Children have thinner skin, meaning hot water causes deeper and much faster damage than it would on an adult. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T6#GNS324_U6_T6_h5)

question: An 80-year-old patient with mild nerve numbness in their hands (neuropathy) is going home. Which safety change is most important?

options.A: Placing heavy glass mugs on the lowest possible counter shelf
options.B: Removing all rugs to prevent tripping and broken bones
options.C: Installing an automatic shut-off timer on the kitchen stove
options.D: Buying a brighter desk lamp for reading in the evening

explanation: You got it! Since neuropathy reduces feeling in the hands, an automatic stove timer prevents them from accidentally leaving burners on or misjudging hot pots. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T6#GNS324_U6_T6_h5)

question: What is the very first thing you should do for someone with a minor burn?

options.A: Cool the burn with running tap water for ten to twenty minutes
options.B: Pop any small blisters immediately to release trapped fluid
options.C: Place crushed ice directly onto the raw wound area
options.D: Apply thick butter or cooking oil to seal the exposed skin

explanation: Correct! Cool running water takes the heat out of the skin fast, stops the burn from going deeper, and eases the pain safely. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T6#GNS324_U6_T6_h6)

question: Why should nurses advise patients NEVER to put butter or toothpaste on a fresh burn?

options.A: They cause the top layer of skin to fall off immediately
options.B: These substances trap heat inside the tissue and can introduce bacteria
options.C: They react chemically with sweat to produce dangerous acid
options.D: They neutralize cool tap water and make the wound freeze faster

explanation: Spot on! Kitchen remedies like butter act like a blanket, keeping the heat trapped inside and inviting germs that cause infections. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T6#GNS324_U6_T6_h6)

question: What is the main goal of community health nurses when it comes to burn safety?

options.A: Preventing burn injuries before they occur through education and hazard reduction
options.B: Training every citizen to operate emergency fire trucks and hoses
options.C: Lowering the financial cost of hospital stays for large insurance companies
options.D: Teaching families how to perform skin grafts in the home environment

explanation: You got it! Prevention is key—teaching families how to spot home hazards stops accidents before they ever happen. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T6#GNS324_U6_T6_h7)

question: A community nurse visits a home with toddlers and spots an unsafe setup. Which finding needs urgent health teaching?

options.A: Hot cups of tea left sitting right near the edge of the dining table
options.B: A working smoke alarm tested and logged on the kitchen wall
options.C: Chemical cleaners stored high up in a locked utility closet
options.D: Pot handles turned inward toward the back of the stove surface

explanation: Spot on! Hot mugs near table edges are a huge scald trap for toddlers who love to reach up and pull things over. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T6#GNS324_U6_T6_h7)
